row.scenario: LQ17 query fixture: the body-only variant of q1 — a word's beginning inside a body word with no help from the title — and the boundary of what a body search finds
row.required_outcome: "what do I prefer?" finds "User prefers kitty over iTerm" through its body alone, as a word beginning (`prefix`); a term inside a body word of a script unicode61 splits into words — Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew … (`presso` in `espresso`; `now` in a Chinese note's `## Knowledge` heading) — finds nothing; a Latin word glued to Chinese text is a whole word (`term`); a literal's last token is a prefix only when it has three or more characters or is a number (`memory_file` finds `memory_files`, `partner's` does not find `partner store`). Supports matrix row 12 and 09 §6.5's measured loss (§6.5.4).

design: §5 step 4 (03 rev 7.8, 09 §6.5.2): the unicode61 table takes every term, its text and phrases split at script boundaries, as a prefix query when its last token has three or more characters (or, 03 rev 7.11, is a number after another token), unless the term carries an unsegmented character or that token is a stop word; the body trigram table holds only chunks carrying a character of a script unicode61 cannot split, and only a term carrying such a character searches it
§5 step 4 (03 rev 7.11's wording): what no table finds is a term inside a word of a body in a script unicode61 splits into words
notes_for_implementer: Seven notes: "Terminal" (the target: its title shares nothing with the question), the espresso decoy, a Chinese note under a `## Knowledge` heading, a Chinese note with `commit` glued to it (`一遍commit`), "Birthday" (`partner's`), "Shopping" (`partner store`) and "Storage crate" (`memory_files`). Step 1: `what`, `do` and `I` are stop words or short and are dropped; `prefer` goes to the unicode61 table as `"prefer"*` and finds the body's `prefers`, which reports `prefix` (not `term`: no token is `prefer`; not `trigram`: no trigram table holds an English body). Step 2 recalls it on the automatic path. Step 3's `prefers` is a whole token, `term`. Step 4's `presso` is inside `espresso` and begins no word, so nothing is found: this is the loss 09 §6.5.4 measures, and a title, an alias or a tag is the remedy. Step 5's `espresso` finds the decoy. Step 6's `now` begins no word and is not searched in the Chinese note's body (a Latin term is matched in a body only as a word or a word's beginning, 09 §6.5.2), so the heading `## Knowledge` does not match. Step 7's `commit` is a whole word once the text is split at the boundary between Chinese and Latin, so it reports `term`. Step 8's `partner's` ends in a one-character token, so it stays the exact phrase `partner s` and does not find `partner store`. Step 9's `memory_file` ends in `file`, which is a prefix, so the phrase `memory file*` finds `memory_files` and reports `phrase`. Steps 8 and 9 each fail under one broken rule: every literal's last token a prefix (8), no literal prefix at all (9).
